What we build for you

Four kinds of work. Each one is backed by a product we designed, built and run ourselves.

  • iOS and native apps

    Apps for iPhone and iPad that feel at home on the device, and keep working without a server where that fits.

    As in DiscVault for iOS

  • Web apps and PWAs

    Web applications that install like an app, work on any screen and can run on your own server.

    As in our self-hosted web apps

  • Websites

    Fast, clear websites that you can keep up to date yourself, from your phone if you like.

    As in Marktkraam.site

  • Advice and self-hosting

    A second pair of eyes on architecture, data ownership and running software yourself with Docker.

    As in self-hosted DiscVault

Proof in our own products

Everything below was designed and built by us, and we still maintain it. It shows what we can build for you.

iOS app and self-hosted platform

DiscVault

A catalogue for physical 4K UHD, Blu-ray and DVD collections. One product in two forms: a standalone iPhone and iPad app that needs no server, and a complete platform you run on your own infrastructure.

What it shows: native iOS, a desktop-first web platform and self-hosting working together in one product.

DiscVault for iOS DiscVault self-hosted

Website platform for market traders

Marktkraam.site

Marktkraam.site gives market traders their own website. Customers see at home what is on the stall today, and the trader updates the offers from a phone.

What it shows: software that people without technical knowledge keep up to date themselves.

Visit Marktkraam.site

Smaller web apps, open on GitHub

Each of these runs on your own server with Docker, so the data stays with you.

  • MealieShopper

    Turns a Mealie week menu into a full basket at Albert Heijn, Picnic or Jumbo.

  • Doorbell Map

    An installable neighbourhood map that shows which houses are happy to receive Halloween visitors.

  • 3D Print Pricing

    Works out what a 3D print really costs, tracks filament stock and turns orders into invoices.

From a first conversation to software you keep

No thick proposals and no surprises. Four steps, and you know where you stand at each one.

  1. 1

    Get to know each other

    You tell us what you want to solve. We ask questions and say honestly whether we are the right fit.

  2. 2

    Proposal

    A concrete plan: what we build, on which platform, what it costs and when it is ready.

  3. 3

    Build

    We build in short rounds. You see working software early and can steer along the way.

  4. 4

    Launch and care

    We deliver, document and stay available for maintenance, or hand everything over so you can run it yourself.

A small studio that builds what it uses

Flux76 is an independent software studio in the Netherlands. We make our own products and take on work for others, and both get the same attention.

You talk directly to the person who builds your software. No account managers, no handovers.

Purpose-built
Each product solves a clear problem without piling on distractions.
Transparent about data
We use only the data a product needs, and make clear what happens to it and who controls it.
The right platform
Native, web or self-hosted: chosen for the job, not for the trend.
Built to last
Clear upgrade paths and software you can keep using for years.
